inputs.interest_income_note: Treasury interest income immaterial ($0.5m) and PGW carries net DEBT, so no interest-income strip. GO-STOCK interest revenue ($8.0m FY2026) is operating income from the livestock financing product and stays in the flows; its funding cost is charged via the net-debt bridge.

inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-25 NZX close, NZD 2.31, verified live by the orchestrating session (Yahoo Finance); regular-session print, not volatile
inputs.wacc_rationale: Additive NZD build: NZ small-cap equity base 11.5% (NZ 10yr govt ~4.5% + ~7pp small-cap equity premium) + 0.75pp earnings cyclicality (farmgate milk price, sheep/beef schedules, on-farm confidence; moderated to 0.75pp because scenario weighting also carries cycle outcomes - risk charged once) + 0.75pp ownership-concentration/governance (Agria ~44% + Elders ~12.3% control >56%; Oct-2025 board ouster briefly breached NZX director rules and forced a trading halt) + 0.5pp illiquidity (market cap ~NZ$174m, well under NZ$300m) = 13.5%. Applied to unlevered flows; deliberately conservative versus a blended E/D WACC (~10.9% at market weights with after-tax debt cost ~5.1%) - the required-return table shows value at lower rates. All rates NZD; flows and price are both NZD.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (mid-cycle variant) per dcf-methods routing - operating company, cyclical distributor/agency; no prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry, fresh build. ANCHOR: FY2026 (30 Jun 2026) actuals, announced 11 Aug 2026. MID-CYCLE FCF: reported FCF is seasonal working-capital noise (FY2017-26 range -$65.5m to +$50.9m) and FY2026's +$46.0m sits near the top with abnormally low capex ($6.6m vs $17-23m run-rate), so the base FCF is component-built: mid-cycle 6.0% EBITDA margin (FY2020-26 avg 6.03%), normalized capex 1.5% of revenue, 28% cash tax, full lease payment charged. LEASE TREATMENT (one treatment, stated): leases as operating cost - the full lease payment (FY2026: $24.03m principal + $4.52m lease interest = $28.55m, 2.66% of revenue) is deducted inside the flows, and lease liabilities ($100.5m at 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt, matching PGW's own net-debt definition (total_debt $92.0m is bank debt only). Not double-counted. Bank interest is NOT in the flows; bank debt is charged once via the net-debt bridge ($88.0m). FY2019 (Seeds sale gain, $333m capital return, 1:10 consolidation) excluded from every average; FY2017-FY2019 not comparable.

mid_cycle_fcf.why_not_reported_fcf: FY2017-26 FCF series (3.4, -17.4, -65.5, 22.4, 50.9, 14.9, 8.3, 34.9, -5.0, 46.0) is dominated by seasonal/cyclical working-capital timing, not earnings power. FY2026's $46.0m combines a working-capital tailwind with a capex holiday ($6.6m vs $17-23m run-rate) and no lease-principal deduction ($24.0m/yr genuine cash obligation sits in financing under IFRS 16). Empirical cross-check: FY2020-26 cumulative dividends $70.5m + Nexan acquisition $19.7m were funded by net debt rising $74.9m - cumulative underlying free cash to shareholders was only ~$15m over six years (~$2.5m/yr), consistent with the ~$13m unlevered mid-cycle figure less ~$4.5m after-tax bank interest and growth working capital.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: cycle-adjusted nominal growth (volumes + inflation) between equity 5yr CAGR (1.0%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (4.8%, flattered by the FY2021 trough base and FY2026 cyclical peak)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.0%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (4.8%) - equity is depressed by dividend payouts, revenue flattered by cyclical recovery. FCF CAGRs are meaningless endpoint noise on a series that swings -$65.5m to +$50.9m; do not use. All CAGRs computed on the post-Seeds FY2020/21-FY2026 window; FY2019 excluded (Seeds sale gain, capital return, 1:10 consolidation).
historical_growth.notes: SBC-zero company: owner-FCF series equals reported FCF less lease principal; no SBC adjustment to history.

scenario_narratives.base: NZ ag mid-cycle: farmgate returns normalize from the FY2026 highs (Fonterra already cut the 2026/27 milk forecast 50c to $9.25/kgMS in Jul-2026), revenue grows ~2-2.5%/yr (volumes + inflation), EBITDA margin holds the FY2020-26 average of 6.0%. Nexan/Blue Ag margin gains offset Farmlands price competition. Working capital (GO-STOCK receivables, inventory) keeps absorbing ~15c per incremental revenue dollar.
scenario_narratives.bull: Commodity strength persists (record $62bn primary exports, strong red meat/dairy), rural real estate and livestock agency - the high-operating-leverage segments - keep inflecting, and vertical integration (Nexan animal-health manufacturing, Blue Ag private label, bidr) lifts the margin to 6.8% (still below the FY2022 peak of 7.05%). Growth 5% fading to 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027-28 downturn: milk price to the low end of Fonterra's $8.00-10.50 range plus El Nino; revenue falls 5% then 3% and agency commissions compress with it. Margin troughs at 4.8% (the FY2024 actual trough), then recovers only to 5.5% - structurally below mid-cycle as Farmlands' below-cost pricing and wool's structural decline bite. Working-capital release cushions the down years.

market_convention_reference.description: Memo, not the house basis: value per share if the terminal value is set AT the scenario's historical EV/EBITDA multiple (bear 4.6x = 10yr min, base 5.1x = FY2020-25 avg, bull 6.2x = max) instead of min(Gordon, cap). This is what the market's own decade-long multiple convention would pay at exit. Even on this basis the DCF sits far below the current price, because ten years of thin interim FCF discounted at 13.5% contributes little and the exit multiple is discounted 3.5x.

simple_multiple_on_current_ebitda.note: Undiscounted multiple math on FY2026 EBITDA - this is roughly how the market prices PGW today. The gap between these figures and the DCF IVs is the EBITDA-to-FCF conversion problem: only ~15-20% of Operating EBITDA converts to owner free cash through the cycle after leases, capex, tax and working capital.

entry_price.note: Entry prices at or below zero are the model speaking plainly: at a 15% hurdle there is no positive price at which the projected owner cash flows fund the return. The stock is only investable at this price on a multiple/asset basis, not on discounted cash flow.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: Fonterra already cut the FY2027 milk-price forecast (Jul-2026), management named commodity pricing and weather (potential El Nino) as the two FY2027 swing factors and declined guidance, and the >56% Agria/Elders bloc has demonstrated abrupt-action risk. Bull cut to 25%: it requires commodity prices to hold AND Nexan/Blue Ag margin capture to land against explicit below-cost price competition from Farmlands.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, the band collapses to a point - band_position is null by design, not 0%.

sanity_check.diagnosis: PASSED - no overvaluation trip. Mid-cycle FCF anchoring and additive WACC premiums were applied pre-emptively (per Step 8c.4/8c.5 guidance) rather than as a post-trip fix, and per-scenario EV/EBITDA exit caps (bear 4.6x / base 5.1x / bull 6.2x) are in place; in the event Gordon terminal values sit far BELOW the caps in every scenario, so the caps never bind.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Pre-emptive: mid-cycle component-built FCF (not the FY2026 $46.0m print), additive WACC 13.5%, exit-multiple caps per scenario.
sanity_check.below_band_note: The check guards against OVER-valuation and passes trivially, because the model lands far BELOW the historical trading band: base-IV implied EV/EBITDA ~1.35x versus a 4.60x ten-year minimum, and implied P/B ~0 versus a 0.90x minimum. The market has priced PGW at 4.6-6.2x EBITDA and 0.9-2.0x book for a decade; discounted owner cash flow supports neither. The divergence is not a model bug - it is the finding (see valuation_philosophy). The reported FY2020-26 cash history (dividends debt-funded, ~$2.5m/yr underlying FCFE) sides with the DCF.

valuation_philosophy: PGW is valued on a mid-cycle owner-FCF basis, not on its reported FY2026 free cash flow of $46m - that print combined a seasonal working-capital tailwind with a capex holiday and, like all IFRS-16 numbers, left the $24m/yr lease principal out of operating cash flow. Through-cycle, PGG Wrightson converts only about $13m of its ~$64m Operating EBITDA into unlevered owner cash: roughly $29m goes to store and saleyard lease payments, ~$16m to normalized capex, ~$7m to tax, and growth working capital (GO-STOCK receivables, inventory on 12-month farmer credit terms) absorbs ~15c of every incremental revenue dollar. That is why a company earning 20.6cps and paying a 10cps dividend can carry a near-zero DCF value: over FY2020-26 the dividends were, in cash terms, funded by $75m of new net debt, not by free cash flow. The market prices PGW the way it prices earnings - 4.6-6.2x EV/EBITDA, around book value ($2.42/share) - which embeds an assumption that the working-capital build is recoverable asset value rather than a perpetual cash sink; the DCF gives no credit for that terminal asset stock. Both views are shown side by side: the house DCF (weighted IV ~$0.05) and the market-convention exit-multiple memo (~$1.21 weighted, $1.86-3.22 on undiscounted current-EBITDA multiple math). At NZD 2.31 the stock is priced at the top of even the market-convention range, offers a negative margin of safety on every cash-flow basis at every discount rate down to 9%, and its dividend depends on the cycle staying friendly and the balance sheet absorbing the working capital. This is a fair-weather earnings-multiple stock, not a discounted-cash-flow investment.
